build.layout: Rear-mid 1.5L 3-cyl turbo plus front e-motor, HV battery under the floor down the middle, carbon (CFRP) passenger cell on aluminum Drive module, dihedral doors
build.summary: Routine oil service is ordinary: the engine is reached from underneath, with the drain plug and cartridge filter together on the sump, so it is not a hard job. Costs rise on hybrid parts (the HV battery sits under the floor in the center of the car and needs HV-certified work), on the carbon passenger cell (bonded CFRP repairs need a BMW-certified body shop), and on the doors, whose gas struts are scheduled replacements. The engine itself is not the problem; the hybrid system and carbon body are.

jobs.why: Done from below on a lift: drain plug in the middle of the sump with the cartridge filter housing right above it; BMW advises dealer service.

The heavy upward-opening doors use gas struts that a specialist replaces at every second oil service.
CFRP panels on the i8 are bonded to the structure, and repairs must follow BMW procedures at certified shops using epoxy that takes 24–50 hours to cure.

name: Porsche Cayman GTS (981)
vs_i8: The Cayman GTS is a smaller, more conventional-looking mid-engine coupe with 340 hp, a naturally aspirated flat-six and an available manual, and it feels sharper and more engaging to drive than the i8. Running costs are ordinary-Porsche rather than hybrid-exotic, the main big risk being a PDK repair, and clean cars sit right around $60k–$65k. GTS values have barely depreciated, so it should hold value better than an i8.

name: Mercedes-Benz G550 (W463)
vs_i8: The old G550 is the boxy icon to the i8's sci-fi supercar: both draw stares, but the G is a 416-hp, 4.0L biturbo V8 brick that is much slower and gets about 13–14 mpg against the i8's plug-in hybrid efficiency. KBB values a 2017 G550 around $54,300, so a clean one fits the $60k budget with room for repairs. Older G-Wagens have already taken their big depreciation hit and lose value slowly, but expect V8-truck running costs and an aging, pre-2019 interior.

recalls.issue: The steering coupling may not be tightened enough and can wear until steering is lost; dealers replace the coupling for free.
The inner door-release cable can break, which could trap occupants after a crash; dealers replace the cables on all four doors.
An ESP fault while Distronic Plus cruise is on may keep engine power from dropping, lengthening stopping distance; fixed with a software reflash.
The brake booster vacuum hose may collapse and make braking harder; dealers replace the hose.
Communication module software may send the wrong location to emergency eCall after a crash; fixed with a free software update.
An eCall software fault can set the wrong date/time and send an inaccurate location to responders; fixed with a software update.

recall_note: 6 NHTSA recalls cover the 2016–2018 G550 (2016 has the most, 2018 only the eCall one), so check by VIN that the steering-coupling, door-cable and brake-hose fixes were done.

name: Lotus Evora 400
vs_i8: The Evora 400 trades the i8's futuristic doors and hybrid tech for a 400-hp supercharged Toyota V6, an available manual, and sharper steering, and clean cars trade right around the $60k mark (KBB fair price about $60,700; recent sales roughly $57k–$72k). Running costs are ordinary-car simple (owners report about $400 a year in routine service) with no high-voltage battery to worry about, but the dealer network is thin and parts can take weeks from the UK. Values have held firm rather than falling like the i8's, though the market is tiny so pricing is noisy.

recalls.issue: The passenger footwell toe board is too flexible, so an unbelted passenger's knee could hit a rigid part in a crash, failing a federal crash standard.

recall_note: NHTSA lists 1 recall for the 2017 Evora 400; confirm by VIN that the toe-board fix was done.

name: Chevrolet Corvette Stingray (C8)
vs_i8: Also a mid-engine head-turner, but quicker than the i8, with a big V8 instead of a hybrid three-cylinder, and dealer service anywhere for much cheaper parts. Used prices are now about $55k–$70k, so it fits a ~$60k budget, and the C8 holds value far better than an i8 (iSeeCars: only 18.7% lost over five years). The main risk is the dual-clutch transmission, so check its filter-service history.

recalls.issue: Rear half-shafts may be missing ball bearings, which can cause sudden loss of drive power; dealers replace the half-shafts.
Contaminated sensor connection can cut the electronic brake boost so the pedal needs much more force; dealers replace the brake boost module.
Driver seat belt retractor may not lock in a crash; dealers replace it.
Front trunk lid can stay unlatched and fly open at speed; software update limits speed to 26 mph when it is unlatched.
Inside front-trunk release button may stop working 10 minutes after shut-off, risking entrapment; fixed with software.
Airbag warning light may come on inconsistently and fail to warn of a fault; fixed with a dealer or over-the-air software update.

recall_note: NHTSA lists 6 recalls across 2020–2022 (4 on 2020 cars, 2 on 2021, 1 on 2022); check the VIN for the half-shaft and brake-boost fixes, and ask for proof of the 2020 valve-spring service bulletin, which is a bulletin, not a recall.

name: Honda Civic Hatchback (10th gen)
vs_i8: The i8 is a $100k+ plug-in-hybrid sports car built around carbon-fiber tub construction and a mid-mounted 3-cylinder hybrid drivetrain; the Civic Hatchback is a sub-$25k-new mainstream commuter car built on a conventional steel unibody with a transverse turbo-4. Running costs aren't comparable: the Civic's insurance, parts, and labor are a fraction of the i8's, and RepairPal rates the Civic's annual repair cost around $368 versus the i8's far higher specialist-shop bills. Where the i8 is a depreciating halo car bought for the experience, the Civic Hatchback is bought to be cheap, reliable transportation, and it holds value better than almost anything else in its class (Honda's hatchback retains roughly 77% of its value after 5 years per iSeeCars). These are simply different categories of car being tracked on the same dashboard for contrast.

model_years.changes: Hatchback body style returns to the US Civic lineup for the first time since 2006, launched exclusively with the 1.5L turbo (174 hp LX/EX/EX-L, 180 hp Sport/Sport Touring).
model_years.recalls: 3 campaigns touch this year (18V266000 seatback pads, 18V663000 steering magnet, 18V817000 owner's manual), plus later fuel-pump and airbag-sensor campaigns

model_years.changes: Minor running changes; Honda Sensing standardized across more trims.
model_years.recalls: Shares the 2017 steering/manual recalls plus the 2018-specific certification-label recall (18V421000) and is within the 20V314000 fuel-pump recall population

model_years.changes: Minor trim/feature shuffle; no major mechanical changes.
model_years.recalls: Covered by the 20V314000 and 21V215000 fuel-pump recalls and the later airbag-sensor recalls; Consumer Reports still rates this year below average

model_years.changes: Mid-cycle refresh: revised front/rear styling, larger touchscreen, Sport trim gets a manual-only option change; reliability improves markedly per Consumer Reports.
model_years.recalls: In the 21V215000 fuel-pump recall, the 23V458000 brake master-cylinder recall, the original 24V064000 airbag-sensor recall, and its 2026 expansion (26V332000)

model_years.changes: Final year of this generation; Coupe body style dropped, Si goes on hiatus for a year, hatchback carries over essentially unchanged with a small price increase; EX-L trim held back.
model_years.recalls: In the 23V458000 brake master-cylinder recall and the 26V332000 airbag-sensor recall

verdict: A well-regarded, practical hatchback that's cheap to insure and maintain once you get past the 2017-2019 cars' known A/C and oil-dilution weak points; 2020-2021 examples are the safer bet. Expect to pay roughly $14,000-$20,000 for a clean 2017-2019 example and high-teens to low-$20,000s for a 2020-2021, depending on trim and mileage — verify all recall work (especially the 2026 airbag-sensor fix) is completed before buying.

EPA combined rating cited as roughly 33-36 mpg depending on trim/transmission, but no annual-cost figure sourced

big_repairs.item: CVT replacement (if neglected or failed outright)

warranty: Factory 3-year/36,000-mile bumper-to-bumper and 5-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranties have expired on all 2017-2021 cars.

Honda's extended A/C condenser/compressor-seal warranty (10 yr/unlimited miles) and the extended 1.5T oil-dilution powertrain warranty may still apply — check VIN history; confirm the 2026 airbag-sensor recall (26V332000) and earlier fuel-pump recalls have been completed.

checklist.check: A/C blows consistently cold on a hot day
checklist.why: Condenser/compressor seal failures are the single most common complaint on this generation

checklist.check: Oil level and condition (check for gasoline smell or overfill on dipstick)
checklist.why: 1.5T oil dilution was a known issue on 2016-2018-built engines; diluted oil smells like fuel and overfills the dipstick

checklist.check: VIN against NHTSA recall lookup for all 10 open/past campaigns
checklist.why: Three overlapping fuel-pump recalls plus a still-active 2026 airbag-sensor recall affect this generation

checklist.check: CVT behavior: smooth power delivery, no flare or shudder under load
checklist.why: CVTs are generally durable but a neglected one is a $3,000+ repair

checklist.check: Interior trim and door/hatch moldings for looseness or rattles
checklist.why: Owner forums report belt moldings and trim rattles as a common, if minor, quality complaint

checklist.check: Service records for recall completion and routine maintenance
checklist.why: Confirms whether known weak points (A/C, fuel pump, airbag sensor) were already addressed

checklist.check: Test full-lock steering turns both directions
checklist.why: 2017-2018 cars included in the 18V663000 power-steering magnet recall

checklist.check: Check-engine or stall history via OBD scan / CarFax
checklist.why: Fuel pump and oil dilution issues can both precede a stall or rough-running complaint

walk_away: No A/C cooling and seller can't show condenser/compressor work was done
Open recalls (especially 26V332000 airbag sensor or the fuel-pump campaigns) not completed and seller unwilling to get them fixed first
Oil that smells strongly of gasoline or is overfilled on the dipstick
CVT shudder, flare, or delayed engagement under load
No maintenance records at all on a 2017-2019 example
